title: Allocator fragmentation fingerprinting & KV-cache shadowing — repro harness and mitigation plan
creator: Priya Menon
description: Intermittent GPU OOMs and long-tail latency spikes observed in high-concurrency end-to-end tests. Root cause appears related to allocator fragmentation combined with KV cache prefetch behavior under continuous batching. This ticket builds a reproducible harness to capture a deterministic fingerprint of fragmentation patterns, documents hypotheses for 'KV-cache shadow' allocations that remain resident across stream boundaries, and proposes mitigations (pool tuning, allocation alignment, and a compaction path).
steps_to_repro: 1) Start dedicated runtime with runtime-1.22 build and runtime flags: --continuous-batching=true --kv-prefetch=true --async-alloc-pool=default
2) Launch 120 parallel worker clients that send batched requests with mixed sequence lengths (short 16 tokens: 70%, medium 256 tokens: 20%, long 1024 tokens: 10%) at sustained QPS for 30 minutes
3) Enable KV warmup (simulate prefetch hits) and intersperse model switches between base/quantized variants every ~5 minutes
4) Collect per-GPU allocator traces (cudaMemPool stats, cudaMallocAsync counters), memory-sampling heap dumps from the runtime, and KV cache prefetch logs
5) Run the harness with different per-stream concurrency (1,4,8) and record fragmentation fingerprints
observed_behavior: After ~10–20 minutes of steady load the system reports growing resident set on GPUs despite steady workload. Memory growth is not monotonic: step increases correlate with model variant rollovers and bursts. cudaMallocAsync arena counts increase, pinned staging allocations spike, and many small leftover allocations (sizes in the 16KB–256KB range) remain resident even after logical KV eviction. Result: transient OOMs and long tail latency due to allocation slow paths.
expected_behavior: With steady throughput and KV eviction enabled, resident GPU memory should stay within expected working set bounds. cudaMallocAsync internal arenas should not grow unbounded, and per-batch allocation churn should be reclaimed by the async pool within a predictable window.
root_cause_hypothesis: A combination of allocation size variance from mixed seq lengths and KV-prefetch allocations created on transient streams is preventing cudaMallocAsync from reusing freed memory effectively. Specifically: (a) small frequent allocations create fragmentation across multiple mempools/arenas; (b) prefetching creates 'shadow' allocations tied to stream lifetime or pinned staging buffers that are not freed synchronously, leaving residue in pools; (c) compaction heuristics are too conservative under continuous batching, so residue accumulates over time.
experiments_run: Pinned staging disabled -> reduces spike magnitude but does not eliminate accumulation
Force synchronous free on eviction path -> immediate reduction in resident but causes latency regressions
Uniform allocation padding to 256B alignment in allocator shim -> reduces number of unique bucket sizes, reduced fragmentation in microbenchmarks
Retain-only-hot-kv-mode (evict aggressively) -> prevents growth but increases cache miss rate and API-level latency
findings: Padding allocations and reducing distinct bucket sizes significantly lowers fragmentation in synthetic runs. Disabling prefetch avoids the shadow residue but is UX-negative. Synchronous frees fix residency but introduce unacceptable tail latency. The allocator's current mempool configuration allows arena proliferation under multistream continuous-batching workloads; compaction thresholds need tuning and a stream-aware free path is missing.
mitigation_plan: Short term: Add a runtime flag to disable KV-prefetch in high-concurrency profiles and roll out to affected fleets (hotfix)
Short term: Apply allocation padding at the runtime allocator shim for small allocations (configurable) to reduce bucket dispersion

Medium term: Implement a 'stream-quarantine' step: when a stream is destroyed, defer one synchronous coalescing pass to return staging/pinned allocations to the pool without blocking inference hot path
Medium term: Tune cudaMallocAsync mempool attributes (max arenas, release thresholds) and expose defaults per deployment class (hosted/dedicated)
Long term: Add a background slab compaction worker that runs opportunistically when GPU utilization < X% and can return large contiguous regions to the OS or consolidate mempools
next_steps: A: Complete reproducible harness and commit to runtime-tests repo (PR opened)
B: Add per-allocation tagging to correlate KV entries to allocator IDs (instrumentation task)
C: Prototype stream-quarantine coalescer in a branch and run soak tests (estimate 2w)
D: Coordinate with SRE to toggle KV-prefetch flag on the limited fleet for canary monitoring
E: Create an observability dashboard tile that shows arena-count, pool-residency, pinned-staging-by-size and correlated KV prefetch events
